- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-1.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion zones; if price is 5%+ above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per period.
- In 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish after day 15, increase forecast slope toward end of horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2% lagged sentiment weight to forecast adjustment.
